messages:
From: Eliot Monroe <eliot@brightline.com>

Subject: Indemnity: responsibility mapping request

Laura —

Thanks for taking this on. Procurement and legal here are trying to lock down the indemnity buckets for the MSA + Order Form. To move the PO and SOW through approvals we need a clear matrix that maps common claim scenarios to: (1) who defends, (2) whether reimbursement/indemnity applies, (3) evidence owners, and (4) expected notice/response SLAs. The key scenarios are: third-party patent assertions, third-party data/privacy claims tied to training data, and alleged infringement arising from model outputs served to end users.

Can you provide a short heatmap (spreadsheet is fine) and call out any scenarios where Redwood would ask Brightline to accept responsibility (e.g., customer-provided data, fine-tuning inputs, integrations)? Also include any carveouts for open-source training data or downstream user misuse.

If possible, share redline-friendly language we can circulate to our GC. We have an internal approval window that closes next week (11/28), so a draft by EOD Tuesday 11/23 would be super helpful. If better to chat, happy to take a 30-min sync.

Attachments: (none yet)

Thanks —
Eliot Monroe

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eliot Monroe <eliot@brightline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity: responsibility mapping request

Eliot —

Thanks — attached is a concise heatmap and a proposed redline (tracked changes) we typically use for commercial customers. High level summary below; please see attachments for the matrix and precise clause language.

Attachments: indemnity_responsibility_heatmap.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed_redlines.docx (docx)

Top-line mapping (draft):
- Third-party patent claims alleging infringement by Redwood models serving Brightline: Redwood will defend and indemnify, provided the claim does not arise from (a) Brightline-provided data or (b) customer fine-tuning instructions that introduce the infringing element.
- Third-party claims tied to Brightline-provided content (uploads, datasets used for fine-tuning): Brightline to defend/indemnify. Redwood to cooperate and provide reasonable technical evidence (logs, model metadata) subject to redaction for confidentiality.
- Alleged infringement from model outputs (end-user prompts + generated content): split approach — Redwood offers indemnity where the output is a direct result of Redwood-controlled model components (base model behavior, operator-configured prompts) and not where the output reproduces Brightline proprietary content. We flag this as the highest-risk bucket and propose an evidence + escrow path in the matrix.

Key requests from our side:
1) Notice window: 30 days after written notice for initial triage; 60 days for final decision to accept defense control.
2) Cooperation clause: mutual obligation to preserve evidence; Redwood can take defense subject to cooperation and control terms we propose in the redline.
3) Insurance/offsets: allow Redwood to seek insurance proceeds and to offset insurance recoveries against indemnity payments (typical waterfall language included).

Kimberly, copying you for legal detail and any alternate language we should include. Ben, please flag any commercial constraints (discount/credits) we might offer to close.

If Brightline can confirm which scenarios are deal-breakers, we can aim to finalize redlines this week and send a DocuSign link for signature alongside the PO.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Legal Operations

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T13:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity: responsibility mapping request

Laura —

Quick legal notes on the draft mapping before we send externally. I inserted tracked changes in proposed_redlines.docx but calling out the substantive asks here so procurement has visibility:

1) Narrow the AI-output indemnity trigger — we should limit Redwood's obligation to outputs that "arise solely from Redwood's model generation absent material Customer-provided content or instructions that reproduce the asserted work." That protects us from prompts that just reproduce customer IP.

2) Add a gross negligence carveout for customer misuse and for attempts to reverse-engineer or redistribute model snapshots. In those cases, no Redwood indemnity.

3) Evidence & notice timeline — we can keep the 30/60 windows but add a "good faith cure" extension (additional 30 days) if Brightline needs time to gather customer evidence; bidirectional cooperation.

4) Defense control & settlement — Redwood will reserve the right to control defense for third-party IP claims where Redwood is indemnifying, but we will not settle any claim that imposes obligations on Brightline without Brightline's written consent.

5) Cap alignment — for Order Form indemnities tied to customer content, recommend a per-claim cap aligned to the Order Form value or a multiple (e.g., 2x). If procurement wants lower caps, we can discuss offsetting commercial concessions.

Ben — if procurement signals that insurance are minimal, we should surface a small one-time onboarding credit (2-4%) to bridge.

Once Laura confirms, I recommend we upload the tracked redline to Drive and send to Brightline with the heatmap and a short bullet summary.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
